title: Recover Binary Search Tree
description:
# Recover Binary Search Tree

You are given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST), where the values of **exactly** two nodes of the tree were swapped by mistake. *Recover the tree without changing its structure*.

Example trees use a level-order display: list the root, then each existing node's left and right children in node order. `null` means an absent child; trailing nulls may be omitted. A tree node stores `val`, `left`, and `right`; tree parameters or return values in code are `TreeNode` objects.

## Example 1:

**Input:** root = [1,3,null,null,2]
**Output:** [3,1,null,null,2]
**Explanation:** 3 cannot be a left child of 1 because 3 > 1. Swapping 1 and 3 makes the BST valid.

## Example 2:

**Input:** root = [3,1,4,null,null,2]
**Output:** [2,1,4,null,null,3]
**Explanation:** 2 cannot be in the right subtree of 3 because 2 < 3. Swapping 2 and 3 makes the BST valid.

## Constraints:

*   The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[2, 1000]`.
*   `-2^31 <= Node.val <= 2^31 - 1`

solutions.name: Inorder Traversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

Traverse the tree in inorder order while keeping the previous visited node. Whenever `prev.val > node.val`, record the first misplaced larger node and keep updating the second misplaced smaller node.

## Key Insight

A valid BST has a sorted inorder sequence. Swapping two values creates either one inversion if the swapped values are adjacent in inorder order, or two inversions if they are separated; `first` should be the first larger node and `second` should be the last smaller node.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)

solutions.name: Morris Inorder Traversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use Morris inorder traversal to visit nodes without recursion or an explicit stack. Temporary threaded links from each predecessor back to the current node let the traversal return after finishing the left subtree.

## Key Insight

The inversion-detection logic is identical to normal inorder traversal; only the traversal mechanism changes. Each temporary thread must be removed before moving right so the tree structure is restored after the scan.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Iterative Stack Inorder
solutions.description:
## Approach

Simulate inorder traversal with an explicit stack. Each time a node is popped, compare it with the previously popped node and record the same first/second inversion candidates used by the recursive method.

## Key Insight

The stack version avoids recursion depth while preserving the exact sorted-order invariant of inorder traversal. It is a good bridge between the recursive solution and the O(1)-space Morris traversal.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)
solutions.code: class Solution { public void recoverTree(TreeNode root) { java.util.Deque<TreeNode> stack = new java.util.ArrayDeque<>(); TreeNode node = root, prev = null, first = null, second = null; while (node != null || !stack.isEmpty()) { while (node != null) { stack.push(node); node = node.left; } node = stack.pop(); if (prev != null && prev.val > node.val) { if (first == null) first = prev; second = node; } prev = node; node = node.right; } int tmp = first.val; first.val = second.val; second.val = tmp; } }

solutions.name: Inorder Node List Repair
solutions.description:
## Approach

Collect all tree nodes into a list using inorder traversal, then scan the list for descending adjacent pairs. Swap the values of the first larger node and the last smaller node found in that list.

## Key Insight

Materializing the inorder sequence makes the inversion pattern explicit. This baseline uses extra space, but it is useful for teaching why the optimized recursive, stack, and Morris variants only need to remember a few nodes.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
solutions.code: class Solution { public void recoverTree(TreeNode root) { java.util.List<TreeNode> nodes = new java.util.ArrayList<>(); inorder(root, nodes); TreeNode first = null, second = null; for (int i = 1; i < nodes.size(); i++) { TreeNode prev = nodes.get(i - 1); TreeNode cur = nodes.get(i); if (prev.val > cur.val) { if (first == null) first = prev; second = cur; } } int temp = first.val; first.val = second.val; second.val = temp; } private void inorder(TreeNode node, java.util.List<TreeNode> nodes) { if (node == null) return; inorder(node.left, nodes); nodes.add(node); inorder(node.right, nodes); } }
